2.8.20.s: māsiśrāddhe tilānāṃ droṇaṃ droṇaṃ yenopāyena śaknuyāt tenopayojayet |
2.8.20.d: मासिश्राद्धे तिलानां द्रोणं द्रोणं येनोपायेन शक्नुयात् तेनोपयोजयेत् ।
2.8.20.e: At every monthly Śrāddha he shall use, in whatever manner he may be able, one droṇa of sesamum.

2.8.20.s: samudetāṃś ca bhojayen na cātadguṇāyocchiṣṭam dadyuḥ |
2.8.20.d: समुदेतांश् च भोजयेन् न चातद्गुणायोच्छिष्टम् दद्युः ।
2.8.20.e: And he shall feed Brāhmaṇas endowed with all (good qualities), and they shall not give the fragments (of the food) to a person who does not possess the same good qualities (as the Brāhmaṇas).

2.8.20.s: udagayana āpūryamāṇapakṣasyaikarātram avarārdhyam upoṣya tiṣyeṇa puṣṭikāmaḥ sthālīpākaṃ śrapayitvā mahārājam iṣṭvā tena sarpiṣmatā brāhmaṇaṃ bhojayitvā puṣṭyarthena siddhiṃ vācayīta |
2.8.20.d: उदगयन आपूर्यमाणपक्षस्यैकरात्रम् अवरार्ध्यम् उपोष्य तिष्येण पुष्टिकामः स्थालीपाकं श्रपयित्वा महाराजम् इष्ट्वा तेन सर्पिष्मता ब्राह्मणं भोजयित्वा पुष्ट्यर्थेन सिद्धिं वाचयीत ।
2.8.20.e: He who desires prosperity shall fast in the half of the year when the sun goes to the north, under the constellation Tishya, in the first half of the month, for (a day and) a night at least, prepare a Sthālīpāka-offering, offer burnt-oblations to Kubera (the god of riches), feed a Brāhmaṇa with that (food prepared for the Sthālīpāka) mixed with clarified butter, and make him wish prosperity with (a Mantra) implying prosperity.

2.8.20.s: evam ahar ahar ā parasmāt tiṣyāt |
2.8.20.d: एवम् अहर् अहर् आ परस्मात् तिष्यात् ।
2.8.20.e: This (rite he shall repeat) daily until the next Tishya(-day).

2.8.20.s: padā pādasya prakṣālanam adhiṣṭhānaṃ ca varjayet |
2.8.20.d: पदा पादस्य प्रक्षालनम् अधिष्ठानं च वर्जयेत् ।

2.8.20.e: And let him spend money on worthy (persons or objects).

2.8.20.s: yantā cātīrthe yato na bhayaṃ syāt |
2.8.20.d: यन्ता चातीर्थे यतो न भयं स्यात् ।
2.8.20.e: And let him not give anything to an unworthy (person), of whom he does not stand in fear.
And let him conciliate men (by gifts or kindness).
And he may enjoy the pleasures which are not forbidden by the holy law.

2.9.21.s: catvāra āśramā gārhasthyam ācāryakulaṃ maunaṃ vānaprasthyam iti |
2.9.21.d: चत्वार आश्रमा गार्हस्थ्यम् आचार्यकुलं मौनं वानप्रस्थ्यम् इति ।
2.9.21.e: There are four orders, viz. the order of householders, the order of students, the order of ascetics, and the order of hermits in the woods.

2.9.21.s: teṣu sarveṣu yathopadeśam avyagro vartamānaḥ kṣemaṃ gacchati |
2.9.21.d: तेषु सर्वेषु यथोपदेशम् अव्यग्रो वर्तमानः क्षेमं गच्छति ।
2.9.21.e: If he lives in all these four according to the rules (of the law), without allowing himself to be disturbed (by anything), he will obtain salvation.
The duty to live in the teacher's house after the initiation is common to all of them.
Not to abandon sacred learning (is a duty common) to all.

2.9.21.s: buddhvā karmāṇi yat kāmayeta tad ārabheta |
2.9.21.d: बुद्ध्वा कर्माणि यत् कामयेत तद् आरभेत ।
2.9.21.e: Having learnt the rites (that are to be performed in each order), he may perform what he wishes.

2.9.21.s: yathā vidyārthasya niyama etenaivāntam anūpasīdata ācāryakule śarīranyāso brahmacāriṇaḥ |
2.9.21.d: यथा विद्यार्थस्य नियम एतेनैवान्तम् अनूपसीदत आचार्यकुले शरीरन्यासो ब्रह्मचारिणः ।
2.9.21.e: Worshipping until death (and living) according to the rule of a (temporary) student, a (professed) student may leave his body in the house of his teacher.
Now (follow the rules) regarding the ascetic (Saṃnyāsin).
Only after (having fulfilled) the duties of that (order of students) he shall go forth (as an ascetic), remaining chaste.
For him (the Saṃnyāsin) they prescribe the following rules).

2.9.21.s: anagnir aniketaḥ syād aśarmāśaraṇo muniḥ | svādhyāyaivotsṛjamāno vācaṃ grāme prāṇavṛttiṃ pratilabhyāniho 'namutraś caret |
2.9.21.d: अनग्निर् अनिकेतः स्याद् अशर्माशरणो मुनिः । स्वाध्यायैवोत्सृजमानो वाचं ग्रामे प्राणवृत्तिं प्रतिलभ्यानिहो ऽनमुत्रश् चरेत् ।
2.9.21.e: He shall live without a fire, without a house, Without pleasures, without protection. Remaining silent and uttering speech only on the occasion of the daily recitation of the Veda, begging so much food only in the village as will sustain his life, he shall wander about neither caring for this world nor for heaven.
It is ordained that he shall wear clothes thrown away (by others as useless).
Some declare that he shall go naked.

2.9.21.s: satyānṛte sukhaduḥkhe vedān imaṃ lokam amuṃ ca parityajyātmānam anvicchet |
2.9.21.d: सत्यानृते सुखदुःखे वेदान् इमं लोकम् अमुं च परित्यज्यात्मानम् अन्विच्छेत् ।
2.9.21.e: Abandoning truth and falsehood, pleasure and pain, the Vedas, this world and the next, he shall seek the Ātman.
(Some say that) he obtains salvation if he knows (the Ātman).
(But) that (opinion) is opposed to the Śāstras.

2.9.21.s: buddhe cet kṣemaprāpaṇam ihaiva na duḥkham upalabheta |
2.9.21.d: बुद्धे चेत् क्षेमप्रापणम् इहैव न दुःखम् उपलभेत ।
2.9.21.e: (For) if salvation were obtained by the knowledge of the Ātman alone, then he ought not to feel any pain even in this (world).
Thereby that which follows has been declared.
Now (follow the rules regarding) the hermit living in the woods.
Only after (completing) that (studentship) he shall go forth, remaining chaste.

2.9.21.s: ekāgnir aniketaḥ syād aśarmāśaraṇo muniḥ | svādhyāya evotsṛjamāno vācam |
2.9.21.d: एकाग्निर् अनिकेतः स्याद् अशर्माशरणो मुनिः । स्वाध्याय एवोत्सृजमानो वाचम् ।

2.9.22.e: A dress of materials procured in the woods (skins or bark) is ordained for him.

2.9.22.s: tato mūlaiḥ phalaiḥ parṇais tṛṇair iti vartayaṃś caret |
2.9.22.d: ततो मूलैः फलैः पर्णैस् तृणैर् इति वर्तयंश् चरेत् ।
2.9.22.e: Then he shall wander about, sustaining his life by roots, fruits, leaves, and grass.
In the end (he shall live on) what has become detached spontaneously.

2.9.22.d: ततो ऽपो वायुम् आकाशम् इत्य् अभिनिश्रयेत् ।
2.9.22.e: Next he shall live on water, (then) on air, then on ether.

2.9.22.s: teṣām uttara uttaraḥ saṃyogaḥ phalato viśiṣṭaḥ |
2.9.22.d: तेषाम् उत्तर उत्तरः संयोगः फलतो विशिष्टः ।
2.9.22.e: Each following one of these modes of subsistence is distinguished by a (greater) reward.
Now some (teachers) enjoin for the hermit the successive performance (of the acts prescribed for the several orders).

2.9.22.s: vidyāṃ samāpya dāraṃ kṛtvāgnīn ādhāya karmāṇy ārabhate somāvarārdhyāni yāni śrūyante |
2.9.22.d: विद्यां समाप्य दारं कृत्वाग्नीन् आधाय कर्माण्य् आरभते सोमावरार्ध्यानि यानि श्रूयन्ते ।
2.9.22.e: After having finished the. study of the Veda, having taken a wife and kindled the sacred fires, he shall begin the rites, which end with the Soma-sacrifices, (performing) as many as are prescribed in the revealed texts.

2.9.22.s: gṛhān kṛtvā sadāraḥ saprajaḥ sahāgnibhir bahir grāmād vaset |
2.9.22.d: गृहान् कृत्वा सदारः सप्रजः सहाग्निभिर् बहिर् ग्रामाद् वसेत् ।
2.9.22.e: (Afterwards) he shall build a dwelling, and dwell outside the village with his wife, his children, and his fires,
Or (he may live) alone.
He shall support himself by gleaning corn.
And after that he shall not any longer take presents.
And he shall sacrifice (only) after having bathed (in the following manner):

2.9.22.s: śanair apo 'bhyaveyād abhighnann abhimukham ādityam udakam upaspṛśet |
2.9.22.d: शनैर् अपो ऽभ्यवेयाद् अभिघ्नन्न् अभिमुखम् आदित्यम् उदकम् उपस्पृशेत् ।
2.9.22.e: He shall enter the water slowly, and bathe without beating it (with his hand), his face turned towards the sun.
This rule of bathing is valid for all (castes and orders).

2.9.22.s: tasya dvaṃdvaṃ dravyāṇām eka upadiśanti pākārthabhojanārthavāsiparaśudātrakājānām |
2.9.22.d: तस्य द्वंद्वं द्रव्याणाम् एक उपदिशन्ति पाकार्थभोजनार्थवासिपरशुदात्रकाजानाम् ।
2.9.22.e: Some enjoin (that he shall prepare) two sets of utensils for cooking and eating, (and) of choppers, hatchets, sickles, and mallets.
He shall take one of each pair (of instruments), give the others (to his wife), and (then) go into the forest.

2.9.22.s: tasyāraṇyenaivāta ūrdhvaṃ homo vṛttiḥ pratīkṣāc chādanaṃ ca |
2.9.22.d: तस्यारण्येनैवात ऊर्ध्वं होमो वृत्तिः प्रतीक्षाच् छादनं च ।
2.9.22.e: After that time (he shall perform) the burnt-oblations, (sustain) his life, (feed) his guests, and (prepare) his clothes with materials produced in the forest.

2.9.22.s: yeṣu karmasu puroḍāśāś caravas teṣu kāryāḥ |
2.9.22.d: येषु कर्मसु पुरोडाशाश् चरवस् तेषु कार्याः ।
2.9.22.e: Rice must be used for those sacrifices for which cakes mixed with meat (are employed by the householder).
And all (the Mantras), as well as the daily portion of the Veda, (must be recited) inaudibly.
He shall not make the inhabitants of the forest hear (his recitation).
(He shall have) a house for his fire (only).
He himself (shall live) in the open air.
His couch and seat, must not be covered (with mats).
If he obtains fresh grain, he shall throw away the old (store).

2.9.23.s: bhūyāṃsaṃ vā niyamam icchann anvaham eva pātreṇa sāyaṃ prātar artham āharet |
2.9.23.d: भूयांसं वा नियमम् इच्छन्न् अन्वहम् एव पात्रेण सायं प्रातर् अर्थम् आहरेत् ।
2.9.23.e: If he desires (to perform) very great austerities, he (shall not make a hoard of grain, but) collect food every day only, morning and evening, in his vessel.

2.9.23.s: tato mūlaiḥ phalaiḥ parṇais tṛṇair iti vartayaṃś cared antataḥ pravṛttāni tato 'po vāyum ākāśam ity abhiniśrayet teṣām uttara uttaraḥ saṃyogaḥ phalato viśiṣṭaḥ |
2.9.23.d: ततो मूलैः फलैः पर्णैस् तृणैर् इति वर्तयंश् चरेद् अन्ततः प्रवृत्तानि ततो ऽपो वायुम् आकाशम् इत्य् अभिनिश्रयेत् तेषाम् उत्तर उत्तरः संयोगः फलतो विशिष्टः ।
2.9.23.e: Afterwards he shall wander about, sustaining his life with roots, fruits, leaves, and grass (which he collects). Finally (he shall content himself with) what has become detached spontaneously. Then he shall live on water, then on air, (and finally) upon ether. Each succeeding mode of subsistence procures greater rewards.
Now they quote (the following) two verses from a Purāṇa:

2.9.23.s: aṣṭāśītisahasrāṇi ye prajām īśirarṣayaḥ | dakṣiṇenāryamṇaḥ panthānaṃ te śmaśānāni bhejire |
2.9.23.d: अष्टाशीतिसहस्राणि ये प्रजाम् ईशिरर्षयः । दक्षिणेनार्यम्णः पन्थानं ते श्मशानानि भेजिरे ।
2.9.23.e: Those eighty thousand sages who desired offspring passed to the south by Aryaman's road and obtained burial-grounds.

2.9.23.s: aṣṭāśītisahasrāṇi ye prajāṃ neṣirarṣayaḥ | uttareṇāryamṇaḥ panthānaṃ te 'mṛtatvaṃ hi kalpate |
2.9.23.d: अष्टाशीतिसहस्राणि ये प्रजां नेषिरर्षयः । उत्तरेणार्यम्णः पन्थानं ते ऽमृतत्वं हि कल्पते ।
2.9.23.e: Those eighty thousand sages who desired no offspring passed by Aryaman's road to the north and obtained immortality.
Thus are praised those who keep the vow of chastity.
Now they accomplish also their wishes merely by conceiving them,

2.9.23.s: yathā varṣaṃ prajādānaṃ dūre darśanaṃ manojavatā yac cānyad evaṃ yuktam |
2.9.23.d: यथा वर्षं प्रजादानं दूरे दर्शनं मनोजवता यच् चान्यद् एवं युक्तम् ।
2.9.23.e: For instance, (the desire to procure) rain, to bestow children, second-sight, to move quick as thought, and other (desires) of this description.

2.9.23.s: tasmāc chrutitaḥ pratyakṣaphalatvāc ca viśiṣṭān āśramān etān eke bruvate |
2.9.23.d: तस्माच् छ्रुतितः प्रत्यक्षफलत्वाच् च विशिष्टान् आश्रमान् एतान् एके ब्रुवते ।
2.9.23.e: Therefore on account of (passages) of the revealed texts, and on account of the visible results, some declare these orders (of men keeping the vow of chastity to be) the most excellent.

2.9.23.s: traividyavṛddhānāṃ tu vedāḥ pramāṇam iti niṣṭhā tatra yāni śrūyante vrīhiyavapaśvājyapayaḥkapālapatnīsaṃbandhāny uccair nīcaiḥ kāryam iti tair viruddha ācāro 'pramāṇam iti manyante |
2.9.23.d: त्रैविद्यवृद्धानां तु वेदाः प्रमाणम् इति निष्ठा तत्र यानि श्रूयन्ते व्रीहियवपश्वाज्यपयःकपालपत्नीसंबन्धान्य् उच्चैर् नीचैः कार्यम् इति तैर् विरुद्ध आचारो ऽप्रमाणम् इति मन्यन्ते ।
2.9.23.e: But (to this we answer): It is the firm opinion of those who are well versed in the threefold sacred learning, that the Vedas are the highest authority. [paragraph continues] They consider that the (rites) which are ordered there to be performed with rice, yava, animals, clarified butter, milk, potsherds, (in conjunction) with a wife, (and accompanied) by loud or muttered (Mantras), must be performed, and that (hence) a rule of conduct which is opposed to these (rites) is of no authority.

2.9.23.s: yat tu śmaśānam ucyate nānākarmaṇām eṣo 'nte puruṣasaṃskāro vidhīyate |
2.9.23.d: यत् तु श्मशानम् उच्यते नानाकर्मणाम् एषो ऽन्ते पुरुषसंस्कारो विधीयते ।
2.9.23.e: But by the term burial-ground (in the text above given) it is intended to ordain the last rites for those who have performed many sacrifices, (and not to mean that dead householders become demons and haunt burial-grounds.)

2.9.23.s: tataḥ param anantyaṃ phalaṃ svargyaśabdaṃ śrūyate |
2.9.23.d: ततः परम् अनन्त्यं फलं स्वर्ग्यशब्दं श्रूयते ।
2.9.23.e: The revealed texts declare that after (the burial follows) a reward without end, which is designated by the term 'heavenly bliss.'

2.9.24.s: athāpy asya prajātim amṛtam āmnāya āha | prajām anu prajāyase tad u te martyāmṛtam iti |
2.9.24.d: अथाप्य् अस्य प्रजातिम् अमृतम् आम्नाय आह । प्रजाम् अनु प्रजायसे तद् उ ते मर्त्यामृतम् इति ।
2.9.24.e: Now the Veda declares also one's offspring to be immortality (in this verse): 'In thy offspring thou art born again, that, mortal, is thy immortality.'

2.9.24.s: athāpi sa evāyaṃ virūḍhaḥ pṛthak pratyakṣeṇopalabhyate dṛśyate cāpi sārūpyaṃ dehatvam evānyat |
2.9.24.d: अथापि स एवायं विरूढः पृथक् प्रत्यक्षेणोपलभ्यते दृश्यते चापि सारूप्यं देहत्वम् एवान्यत् ।
2.9.24.e: Now it can also be perceived by the senses that the (father) has been reproduced separately (in the son); for the likeness (of a father and of a son) is even visible, only (their) bodies are different.

2.9.24.s: te śiṣṭeṣu karmasu vartamānāḥ pūrveṣāṃ sāṃparāyeṇa kīrtiṃ svargaṃ ca vardhayanti |
2.9.24.d: ते शिष्टेषु कर्मसु वर्तमानाः पूर्वेषां सांपरायेण कीर्तिं स्वर्गं च वर्धयन्ति ।
2.9.24.e: 'These (sons) who live, fulfilling the rites taught (in the Veda), increase the fame and heavenly bliss of their departed ancestors.'
'In this manner each succeeding (generation increases the fame and heavenly bliss) of the preceding ones.'
'They (the ancestors) live in heaven until the (next) general destruction of created things.'
At the new creation (of, the world) they become the seed. That has been declared in the Bhavishyatpurāṇa.
Now Pra g āpati also says,

2.9.24.s: trayīṃ vidyāṃ brahmacaryaṃ prajātiṃ śraddhāṃ tapo yajñam anupradānam | ya etāni kurvate tair it saha smo rajo bhūtvā dhvaṃsate 'nyat praśaṃsann iti |
2.9.24.d: त्रयीं विद्यां ब्रह्मचर्यं प्रजातिं श्रद्धां तपो यज्ञम् अनुप्रदानम् । य एतानि कुर्वते तैर् इत् सह स्मो रजो भूत्वा ध्वंसते ऽन्यत् प्रशंसन्न् इति ।
2.9.24.e: 'Those dwell with us who fulfil the following (duties): the study of the three Vedas, the studentship, the procreation of children, faith, religious austerities, sacrifices, and the giving of gifts. He who praises other (duties), becomes dust and perishes.'

2.9.24.s: tatra ye pāpakṛtas ta eva dhvaṃsanti yathā parṇaṃ vanaspater na parān hiṃsanti |
2.9.24.d: तत्र ये पापकृतस् त एव ध्वंसन्ति यथा पर्णं वनस्पतेर् न परान् हिंसन्ति ।
2.9.24.e: Those among these (sons) who commit sin, perish alone, just as the leaf of a tree (which has been attacked by worms falls without injuring its branch or tree). They do not hurt their ancestors.

2.9.24.s: nāsyāsmiṃl loke karmabhiḥ saṃbandho vidyate tathā parasmin karmaphalaiḥ |
2.9.24.d: नास्यास्मिंल् लोके कर्मभिः संबन्धो विद्यते तथा परस्मिन् कर्मफलैः ।
2.9.24.e: (For) the (ancestor) has no connection with the acts committed (by his descendant) in this world, nor with their results in the next.
(The truth of) that may be known by the following (reason):
This creation (is the work) of Pra g āpati and of the sages.

2.9.24.s: tatra ye puṇyakṛtas teṣāṃ prakṛtayaḥ parā jvalantya upalabhyante |
2.9.24.d: तत्र ये पुण्यकृतस् तेषां प्रकृतयः परा ज्वलन्त्य उपलभ्यन्ते ।
2.9.24.e: The bodies of those (sages) who stay there (in heaven) on account of their merits appear visibly most excellent and brilliant (as, for instance, the constellation of the seven Ri shis).

2.9.24.s: syāt tu karmāvayavena tapasā vā kaścit saśarīro 'ntavantaṃ lokaṃ jayati saṃkalpasiddhiś ca syān na tu taj jyaiṣṭhyam āśramāṇām |
2.9.24.d: स्यात् तु कर्मावयवेन तपसा वा कश्चित् सशरीरो ऽन्तवन्तं लोकं जयति संकल्पसिद्धिश् च स्यान् न तु तज् ज्यैष्ठ्यम् आश्रमाणाम् ।
2.9.24.e: But even though some (ascetic), whilst still in the body, may gain heaven through a portion of (the merit acquired by his former) works or through austerities, and though he may. accomplish (his objects) by his mere wish, still this is no reason to place one order before the other.

2.9.25.s: vyākhyātāḥ sarvavarṇānāṃ sādhāraṇavaiśeṣikā dharmāḥ | rājñas tu viśeṣād vakṣyāmaḥ |
2.9.25.d: व्याख्याताः सर्ववर्णानां साधारणवैशेषिका धर्माः । राज्ञस् तु विशेषाद् वक्ष्यामः ।

2.9.25.s: tasya purastād āvasathas tad āmantraṇam ity ācakṣate |
2.9.25.d: तस्य पुरस्ताद् आवसथस् तद् आमन्त्रणम् इत्य् आचक्षते ।

2.9.25.s: dakṣiṇena puraṃ sabhā dakṣiṇodagdvārā yathobhayaṃ saṃdṛśyeta bahir antaraṃ ceti |
2.9.25.d: दक्षिणेन पुरं सभा दक्षिणोदग्द्वारा यथोभयं संदृश्येत बहिर् अन्तरं चेति ।

2.9.25.s: teṣāṃ yathāguṇam āvasathāḥ śayyānnapānaṃ ca videyam |
2.9.25.d: तेषां यथागुणम् आवसथाः शय्यान्नपानं च विदेयम् ।

2.9.25.s: na cāsya viṣaye kṣudhā rogeṇa himātapābhyāṃ vāvasīded abhāvād buddhipūrvaṃ vā kaścit |
2.9.25.d: न चास्य विषये क्षुधा रोगेण हिमातपाभ्यां वावसीदेद् अभावाद् बुद्धिपूर्वं वा कश्चित् ।

2.9.25.s: sabhāyā madhye 'dhidevanam uddhatyāvokṣyākṣān nivaped yugmān vaibhītakān yathāarthān |
2.9.25.d: सभाया मध्ये ऽधिदेवनम् उद्धत्यावोक्ष्याक्षान् निवपेद् युग्मान् वैभीतकान् यथाअर्थान् ।
आयुधग्रहणं नृत्तगीतवादित्राणीति राजाधीनेभ्यो ऽन्यत्र न विद्येरन् ।

2.9.25.s: kṣemakṛd rājā yasya viṣaye grāme 'raṇye vā taskarabhayaṃ na vidyate |
2.9.25.d: क्षेमकृद् राजा यस्य विषये ग्रामे ऽरण्ये वा तस्करभयं न विद्यते ।

2.10.26.s: bhṛtyānām anuparodhena kṣetraṃ vittaṃ ca dadad brāhmaṇebhyo yathārham anantāṃl lokān abhijayati |
2.10.26.d: भृत्यानाम् अनुपरोधेन क्षेत्रं वित्तं च ददद् ब्राह्मणेभ्यो यथार्हम् अनन्तांल् लोकान् अभिजयति ।
2.10.26.e: A (king) who, without detriment to his servants, gives land and money to Brāhmaṇas according to their deserts gains endless worlds.

2.10.26.s: brāhmaṇasvāny apajigīṣamāṇo rājā yo hanyate tam āhur ātmayūpo yajño 'nantadakṣiṇa iti |
2.10.26.d: ब्राह्मणस्वान्य् अपजिगीषमाणो राजा यो हन्यते तम् आहुर् आत्मयूपो यज्ञो ऽनन्तदक्षिण इति ।
2.10.26.e: They say (that) a king, who is slain in attempting to recover the property of Brāhmaṇas, (performs) a sacrifice where his body takes the place of the sacrificial post, and at which an unlimited fee is given.

2.10.26.s: etenānye śūrā vyākhyātāḥ prayojane yudhyamānās tanutyajaḥ |
2.10.26.d: एतेनान्ये शूरा व्याख्याताः प्रयोजने युध्यमानास् तनुत्यजः ।
2.10.26.e: Hereby have been declared (the rewards of) other heroes, who fall fighting for a (worthy) cause.

2.10.26.s: grāmeṣu nagareṣu cāryāñ śucīn satyaśīlān prajāguptaye nidadhyāt |
2.10.26.d: ग्रामेषु नगरेषु चार्याञ् शुचीन् सत्यशीलान् प्रजागुप्तये निदध्यात् ।
2.10.26.e: He shall appoint men of the first three castes, who are pure and truthful, over villages and towns for the protection of the people.
Their servants shall possess the same qualities.
They must protect a town from thieves in every direction to the distance of one yo g ana.
(They must protect the country to the distance of) one krośa from each village.

2.10.26.s: tatra yan muṣyate tais tat pratidāpyam |
2.10.26.d: तत्र यन् मुष्यते तैस् तत् प्रतिदाप्यम् ।
2.10.26.e: They must be made to repay what is stolen within these (boundaries).
The (king) shall make them collect the lawful taxes ( s ulka).
A learned Brāhmaṇa is free from taxes,
And the women of all castes,
And male children before the marks (of puberty appear),
And those who live (with a teacher) in order to study,
And those who perform austerities, being intent on fulfilling the sacred law,
And a Śūdra who lives by washing the feet,
Also blind, dumb, deaf, and diseased persons (as long as their infirmities last),
And those to whom the acquisition of property is forbidden (as Sannyāsins).

2.10.26.s: abuddhipūrvam alaṃkṛto yuvā paradāram anupraviśan kumārīṃ vā vācā bādhyaḥ |
2.10.26.d: अबुद्धिपूर्वम् अलंकृतो युवा परदारम् अनुप्रविशन् कुमारीं वा वाचा बाध्यः ।
2.10.26.e: A young man who, decked with ornaments, enters unintentionally (a place where) a married woman or a (marriageable) damsel (sits), must be reprimanded.
But he does it intentionally with a bad purpose, he must be fined.
If he has actually committed adultery, his organ shall be cut off together with the testicles.
But (if he has had intercourse) with a (marriageable) girl, his property shall be confiscated and he shall be banished.
Afterwards the king must support (such women and damsels),
And protect them from defilement.
If they agree to undergo the (prescribed) penance, he shall make them over to their (lawful) guardians.

2.10.27.e: If (adulteresses) have performed (the prescribed penance), they are to be treated as before (their fault). For the connection (of husband and wife) takes place through the law.
(A husband) shall not make over his (wife), who occupies the position of a 'gentilis,' to others (than to his 'gentiles'), in order to cause children to be begot for himself.

2.10.27.s: kulāya hi strī pradīyata ity upadiśanti |
2.10.27.d: कुलाय हि स्त्री प्रदीयत इत्य् उपदिशन्ति ।
2.10.27.e: For they declare, that a bride is given to the family (of her husband, and not to the husband alone).
That is (at present) forbidden on account of the weakness of (men's) senses.
The hand (of a gentilis is considered in law to be) that of a stranger, and so is (that of any other person except the husband).
If the (marriage vow) is transgressed, both (husband and wife) certainly go to hell.

2.10.27.s: niyamārambhaṇo hi varṣīyān abhyudaya evam ārambhaṇād apatyāt |
2.10.27.d: नियमारम्भणो हि वर्षीयान् अभ्युदय एवम् आरम्भणाद् अपत्यात् ।
2.10.27.e: The reward (in the next world) resulting from obeying the restrictions of the law is preferable to offspring obtained in this manner (by means of Niyoga).
A man of one of the first three castes (who commits adultery) with a woman of the Śūdra caste shall be banished.
A Śūdra (who commits adultery) with a woman of one of the first three castes shall suffer capital punishment.
And he shall emaciate a woman who has committed adultery with a ( Śūdra, by making her undergo penances and fasts, in case she had no child).

2.10.27.s: savarṇāyām anyapūrvāyāṃ sakṛt saṃnipāte pādaḥ patatīty upadiśanti |
2.10.27.d: सवर्णायाम् अन्यपूर्वायां सकृत् संनिपाते पादः पततीत्य् उपदिशन्ति ।
2.10.27.e: They declare, that (a Brāhmaṇa) who has once committed adultery with a married woman of equal class, she perform one-fourth of the penance prescribed for an outcast.
In like manner for every repetition (of the crime), one-fourth of the penance (must be added).
(If the offence be committed) for the fourth time, the whole (penance of twelve years must be performed).
The tongue of a Śūdra who speaks evil of a virtuous person, belonging to one of the first three castes, shall be cut out.

2.10.27.s: vāci pathi śayyāyām āsana iti samībhavato daṇḍatāḍanam |
2.10.27.d: वाचि पथि शय्यायाम् आसन इति समीभवतो दण्डताडनम् ।
2.10.27.e: A Śūdra who assumes a position equal (to that of a member of one of the first three castes), in conversation, on the road, on a couch, in sitting (and on similar occasions), shall be flogged.

2.10.27.s: puruṣavadhe steye bhūmyādāna iti svāny ādāya vadhyaḥ |
2.10.27.d: पुरुषवधे स्तेये भूम्यादान इति स्वान्य् आदाय वध्यः ।
2.10.27.e: In case (a Śūdra) commits homicide or theft, appropriates land (or commits similar heinous crimes), his property shall be confiscated and he himself shall suffer capital punishment.
But if these (offences be committed) by a Brāhmaṇa, he shall be made blind (by tying a cloth over his eyes).
He shall keep in secret confinement him who violates the rules (of his caste or order), or any other sinner, until (he promises) amendment.
If he does not amend, he shall be banished.

2.10.27.s: ācārya ṛtvik snātako rājeti trāṇaṃ syur anyatra vadhyāt |
2.10.27.d: आचार्य ऋत्विक् स्नातको राजेति त्राणं स्युर् अन्यत्र वध्यात् ।

2.11.28.s: kṣetraṃ parigṛhyotthānābhāvāt phalābhāve yaḥ samṛddhaḥ sa bhāvi tad apahāryaḥ |
2.11.28.d: क्षेत्रं परिगृह्योत्थानाभावात् फलाभावे यः समृद्धः स भावि तद् अपहार्यः ।
2.11.28.e: If a person who has taken (a lease of) land (for cultivation) does not exert himself, and hence (the land) bears no crop, he shall, if he is rich, be made to pay (to the owner of the land the value of the crop) that ought to have grown.
A servant in tillage who abandons his work shall be flogged.
The same (punishment shall be awarded) to a herdsman (who leaves his work);
And the flock (entrusted) to him shall be taken away (and be given to some other herdsman).

2.11.28.s: hitvā vrajam ādinaḥ karśayet paśūn nātipātayet |
2.11.28.d: हित्वा व्रजम् आदिनः कर्शयेत् पशून् नातिपातयेत् ।
2.11.28.e: If cattle, leaving their stable, eat (the crops of other persons, then the owner of the crops, or the king's servants), may make them lean (by impounding them); (but) he shall not exceed (in such punishment).

2.11.28.s: avarudhya paśūn māraṇe nāśane vā svāmibhyo 'vasṛjet |
2.11.28.d: अवरुध्य पशून् मारणे नाशने वा स्वामिभ्यो ऽवसृजेत् ।
2.11.28.e: If (a herdsman) who has taken cattle under his care, allows them to perish, or loses (them by theft, through his negligence), he shall replace them (or pay their value) to the owners.

2.11.28.s: pramādād araṇye paśūn utsṛṣtān dṛṣṭvā grāmam ānīya svāmibhyo 'vasṛjet |
2.11.28.d: प्रमादाद् अरण्ये पशून् उत्सृष्तान् दृष्ट्वा ग्रामम् आनीय स्वामिभ्यो ऽवसृजेत् ।
2.11.28.e: If (the king's forester) sees cattle that have been sent into the forest through negligence (without a herdsman), he shall lead them back to the village and make them over to the owners.
If the same negligence (occur) again, he shall once impound them (and afterwards give them back).
(If the same fault be committed again) after that (second time), he shall not take care (of them).

2.11.28.s: paraparigraham avidvān ādadāna edhodake mūle puṣpe phale gandhe grāse śāka iti vācā bādhyaḥ |
2.11.28.d: परपरिग्रहम् अविद्वान् आददान एधोदके मूले पुष्पे फले गन्धे ग्रासे शाक इति वाचा बाध्यः ।
2.11.28.e: He who has taken unintentionally the property of another shall be reprimanded, in case (the property be) fuel, water, roots, flowers, fruits, perfumes, fodder, or vegetables.
(If he takes the above-mentioned kinds of property) intentionally, his garment shall be taken away.

2.11.28.s: adaṇḍyaḥ kāmakṛte tathā prāṇasaṃśaye bhojanam ādadānaḥ |
2.11.28.d: अदण्ड्यः कामकृते तथा प्राणसंशये भोजनम् आददानः ।
2.11.28.e: He who takes intentionally food when he is in danger of his life shall not be punished.
If the king does not punish a punishable offence, the guilt falls upon him.

2.11.29.s: prayojayitā mantā karteti svarganarakaphaleṣu karmasu bhāginaḥ |
2.11.29.d: प्रयोजयिता मन्ता कर्तेति स्वर्गनरकफलेषु कर्मसु भागिनः ।
2.11.29.e: He who instigates to, he who assists in, and he who commits (an act, these three) share its rewards in heaven and its punishments in hell.
He amongst these who contributes most to the accomplishment (of the act obtains) a greater share of the result.
Both the wife and the husband have power over (their) common property.

2.11.29.d: तयोर् अनुमते ऽन्ये ऽपि तद् हितेषु वर्तेरन् ।
2.11.29.e: By their permission, others also may act for their good (in this and the next world, even by spending money).

2.11.29.s: vivāde vidyābhijanasaṃpannā vṛddhā medhāvino dharmeṣv avinipātinaḥ |
2.11.29.d: विवादे विद्याभिजनसंपन्ना वृद्धा मेधाविनो धर्मेष्व् अविनिपातिनः ।
2.11.29.e: Men of learning and pure descent, who are aged, clever in reasoning, and careful in fulfilling the duties (of their caste and order, shall be the judges) in lawsuits.
In doubtful cases (they shall give their decision) after having ascertained (the truth) by inference, ordeals, and the like (means).

2.11.29.s: puṇyāhe prātar agnāv iddhe 'pāmante rājavaty ubhayataḥ samākhyāpya sarvānumate mukhyaḥ satyaṃ praśnaṃ brūyāt |
2.11.29.d: पुण्याहे प्रातर् अग्नाव् इद्धे ऽपामन्ते राजवत्य् उभयतः समाख्याप्य सर्वानुमते मुख्यः सत्यं प्रश्नं ब्रूयात् ।
2.11.29.e: A person who is possessed of good qualities (may be called as a witness, and) shall answer the questions put to him according to the truth on an auspicious day, in the morning, before a kindled fire, standing near (a jar full of) water, in the presence of the king, and with the consent of all (of both parties and of the assessors), after having been exhorted (by the judge) to be fair to both sides.
If (he is found out speaking) an untruth, the king shall punish him.
Besides, in that case, after death, hell (will be his punishment).
If he speaks the truth, (his reward will be) heaven and the approbation of all created beings.

2.11.29.s: sā niṣṭhā yā vidyā strīṣu śūdreṣu ca |
2.11.29.d: सा निष्ठा या विद्या स्त्रीषु शूद्रेषु च ।
2.11.29.e: The knowledge which Śūdras and women possess is the completion (of all study).
They declare, that (this knowledge) is a supplement of the Atharva-Veda.

2.11.29.s: kṛcchrā dharmasamāptiḥ samāmnātena | lakṣaṇakarmaṇāt tu samāpyate |
2.11.29.d: कृच्छ्रा धर्मसमाप्तिः समाम्नातेन । लक्षणकर्मणात् तु समाप्यते ।
2.11.29.e: It is difficult to learn the sacred law from (the letter of) the Vedas (only); but by following the indications it is easily accomplished.

2.11.29.s: tatra lakṣaṇam | sarvajanapadeṣv ekāntasamāhitam āryāṇāṃ vṛttaṃ samyagvinītānāṃ vṛddhānām ātmavatām alolupānām adāmbhikānāṃ vṛttasādṛśyaṃ bhajeta | evam ubhau lokāv abhijayati |
2.11.29.d: तत्र लक्षणम् । सर्वजनपदेष्व् एकान्तसमाहितम् आर्याणां वृत्तं सम्यग्विनीतानां वृद्धानाम् आत्मवताम् अलोलुपानाम् अदाम्भिकानां वृत्तसादृश्यं भजेत । एवम् उभौ लोकाव् अभिजयति ।
2.11.29.e: The indications for these (doubtful cases are), 'He shall regulate his course of action according to the conduct which is unanimously recognised in all countries by men of the three twice-born castes, who have been properly obedient (to their teachers), who are aged, of subdued senses, neither given to avarice, nor hypocrites. Acting thus he will gain both worlds.'

2.11.29.s: strībhyaḥ sarvavarṇebhyaś ca dharmaśeṣān pratīyād ity eka ity eke |
2.11.29.d: स्त्रीभ्यः सर्ववर्णेभ्यश् च धर्मशेषान् प्रतीयाद् इत्य् एक इत्य् एके ।
2.11.29.e: Some declare, that the remaining duties (which have not been taught here) must be learnt from women and men of all castes.
